entities.summary: Fauvism was an influential early 20th-century art movement that revolutionized the way artists approached color and composition. Emerging around 1904 CE in Paris, France, this avant-garde style emphasized painterly qualities and strong color over representational or realistic values retained by Impressionism. The movement's key figures, including Henri Matisse and André Derain, sought to break free from traditional techniques and create a new visual language. Their innovations had a profound impact on modern art, influencing subsequent movements such as Expressionism and Fauvist-inspired styles. As a result, Fauvism played a significant role in shaping the development of modern art, leaving a lasting legacy in the world of visual arts.
